lines.text: Welcome to Pirate Quest! Set sail, gather your crew, and battle rival captains. Every choice shapes your journey—will you rule the seas or be lost to the depths? Are you ready to begin your quest?
Are you ready to begin your quest?
Are you ready to begin your quest?
Begin your pirate adventure another time.
Ahoy, Captain. Ye look like ye wrestled a kraken last night and lost. But I bring good tidings. One of our lads, bless his terrible luck in dice, stumbled upon something, a treasure map.
What's the plan, Cap'n? Say: map, or supplies.
What will you do? Say: MAP, or, Supplies.
You can say: Map, or, Supplies.
Yes, yes. Let's gather supplies, food and drink for our voyage.
Tasty tropical punch. Get your tasty tropical punch right here.
Oh, yes. Hmm, what's down this alleyway? There's a man sitting mysteriously.
You ever heard of the Devil's Triangle? Aye, I sailed through it blindfolded and came out laughing
He sounds experienced. Should we: Recruit, or learn?
You can say: RECRUIT, or LEARN
You use your map, and get sailing instantly.
Smooth waters, clear skies. Aye, if that ain't a good omen, I don't know what is. Though something about it feels almost too good. It's an enemy pirate ship. Arrr.
What's the call, Cap'n? Fight, Flee, or Talk?
You can say FIGHT, FLEE, or TALK
Let's show them what we've got. Load the cannons. Nice shot. You hit their ship. Oh. Take cover. They hit us.
Captain, we aren't made of steel
What's your choice. board, or flee?
You can say: BOARD, or FLEE
Let's board the enemy ship. There are enemy pirates.
The fight is on. Took that enemy pirate out. Who is this?
I am the captain of this vessel.
You can say: DUEL, or BRUTAL
Think you can take my ship? Let's see what you're made of.
En garde. Time to duel. Argh.
No honour in that. You decide to spare him, and take his ship.
Good job captain. Now, are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Want to sail to treasure island?
Captain, how could you do this?
We've won the battle, but at what cost? Some fine men won't be raising their mugs tonight.
Good job captain. Now, are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Want to sail to treasure island?
Turn the sails. Catch the wind. That was close, but we've caught the wind now, Captain. They'll never catch us. That's a tale for the tavern. But maybe next time we fight first
Good job captain. Now, are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Want to sail to treasure island?
I'll shout to the other boat, "Give us all your cargo and supplies unless you fancy a swim."
Tempting, but how about this? I'll give you some of my goods, but in return, you owe me a favor down the line, a real pirate's debt.
Careful, Captain, a pirate's debt always comes due, and it ain't paid in gold. It's paid in trouble
A pleasure doing business, Captain. Just remember, one day I might come collect that favor.
Aye, Captain. Taking a pirate's tithe for some goods. Next you'll be telling me we're starting a charity
Good job captain. Now, are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Are you ready to sail onto treasure island?
Time to find Treasure Island. But maybe a nice shanty first.
A hi-di, hi-di, hi-di-ho. A hi-di-ho. A hi-di-ho. A hi-di, hi-di, hi-di-ho, over the deep blue sea.
There it is in the distance, a jungle covered island.
Aye, Captain, that be the place. Treasure waits for no man
Say Yes, to drop the anchor and go ashore.
Fine. Instead of dropping the anchor, let's sing another shanty.
Hi-di, hi-di, hi-di, ho. A hi-di, ho. A hi-di, ho. A hi-di, hi-di, hi-di, ho. Over the deep blue sea
Are you ready to drop the anchor?
Are you ready to drop the anchor?
The anchor rope is nice and tight. Let's investigate this jungle. Lots of bushy trees here. We are lost. I think our ship navigator has made a mistake.

Captain, this treasure map, it's old. The landmarks don't match exactly, and there be signs of shifting tides. I just need a bit of time to find the right way. I got it. Follow me deeper into the jungle
Would you like to follow the navigator?
Would you like to follow the navigator?
Would you like to follow the navigator?
Give me that map, navigator. Hmm. This way, through the jungle.
After hours of trekking, the trees thin out. You spot something through the leaves — a wrecked ship, half-buried in the sand. You see a familiar face.
It is I, Barnacle Joe. You must have the same eye for treasure as me and me crew. It's magnificent. I tell you what, we can split it fairly, 100 gold coins each, and then part ways
What will ye do, Cap'n? Say: SPLIT, or FIGHT.
You can say SPLIT, or FIGHT.
Let's explore this jungle a bit. There's a monkey eating a scrumptious banana.
Well, that was exciting. It's high time we go back to the ship
Are you ready to go back to the ship?
Are you ready to go back to the ship?
Want to go back to your ship?
Haha, smart choice, Captain. There's your share of the treasure, 100 gold coins.
That wasn't very piratey of you, Captain. Well, at least you got your share. Let's go back to the high seas
Want to go back to your ship?
Want to go back to your ship?
Want to go back to your ship?
Oh, I see how it is. Feel the wrath of my fish cannon. Fire!
Ouch, a fish to the face. Captain, you know what to do.
You impaled all my fish. Fine, have it your way. Take all the treasure.
Great job, Captain. Let's go back to the ship with our plunder
Are you ready to return to the ship?
Are you ready to return to the ship?
Are you ready to return to the ship?
Fine, navigator, lead the way. I hope this doesn't end up in us being dinner for some jungle beast.
Well, I'll be a bilge rat's uncle. Look at that, a pile of glorious treasure.
You take the coins and head back to the ship. Time to continue your adventure. Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Let's set sail. Captain, something doesn't seem right. There's a weird smell in the air.
Either this ship's haunted or Mad Jack's been cooking again.
Captain, this treasure be cursed. Perhaps we should find a shaman to help lift the curse
What's yer call, Cap'n? Want to seek a shaman to help with the curse?
Want to seek a shaman to help lift the curse?
Want to seek a shaman to help lift the curse?
I agree, Captain. Ghost stories, how ridiculous. We keep sailing. Ugh, this food is all rotten. Where did all the sound go? Maybe just a coinc- It's the ghost, Captain
This isn't good. Let's hear what the ghost captain has to say.
I am the Ghost Captain. Mortals, you have taken treasure that is not yours. You must pay for your actions
Well, someone got out of the wrong side of bed this morning. Captain. What will you do. Fight, or flee?
What will you do. Fight, or flee?
You can say: FIGHT or FLEE.
This will be a battle for the ages. Attack! Our cutlasses are ineffective.
Foolish mortals. You cannot destroy what is already dead. We reclaim this treasure
The ghosts took the treasure. Atleast you live to tell the tale.
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Well, since you don't want to set sail, here is a joke to warm your cockles
Why did the pirate go to the seafood restaurant? Because he heard they had great fish and chips.
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Good choice, Captain. Fightin' ghosts, it ain't smart. Let's hightail it out of here. Yes, we're catching the wind.
You escape the ghosts, but your treasure mysteriously vanishes. Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
There's only one place with a shaman, Skull Island. Here we are.
A shrouded figure appears from the mist, a wooden staff in one hand, bones clinking from her belt.
I saw you coming. I am the shaman of Skull Island. I can lift your pirate's curse, but you must sacrifice one of your men
Want to give the shaman a member of your crew?
Want to give a member of your crew?
I fought for you, Captain. Don't give me to the shaman.
Too late. Your misfortune has been decided. Your treasure's curse is now lifted.
Morale is shattered. The crew won't forget this choice, Captain
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
You don't sacrifice one of your men, and offer the shaman coins instead.
Hmm. I accept your offering. I will remove your treasure's curse. All done.
Well done, captain. You lost a lot of coins, but you stayed true to your men
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
The cursed mist fades, and the open sea stretches before ye once more.
Captain, the crew is tired. They haven't had a hot meal or proper bed in weeks.
We need a town, a place to drink, a place to spend our hard-earned gold.
There's a pirate haven near Tortuga's nastier cousin. We dock there, the crew gets their fill, and we rest before the next storm
What do you say captain. Want to sail to the pirate haven?
Want to sail to the pirate haven?
Want to sail to the pirate haven?
Before going to the haven, let's enjoy a lovely shanty
Hi-di, hi-di, hi-di, ho. A hi-di-ho. A hi-di-ho. A hi-di, hi-di, hi-di, ho. Over the deep blue sea
That really hit the spot. Now, we should really go to that haven
You pull in close to the haven.
Welcome to Dead Man's Refuge. A place where even the governor wouldn't dare show his face.
Now, you are in the haven. There are two things to do. Would you like to rest, or play dice?
You can say REST, or DICE.
Welcome to Dead Man's Refuge. A place where even the governor wouldn't dare show his face.
Now, you are in the haven. There are two things to do. Would you like to rest, or play dice?
You can say REST, or DICE.
The warmth of the inn welcomes ye. A roaring fire, a soft bed, and a cup of tropical punch smoother than the sea on a calm day. Sleep well, Captain.
You awake, well rested. You gain 20 health, but spend 10 coins in the process.
Are you ready to rejoin the crew?
Are you ready to rejoin the crew?
Are you ready to rejoin the crew?

The sea gods smile on ye today, Captain
A tie. Ain't that something? Looks like the sea gods can't decide. Try your luck again, captain
Your coin pouch is empty. No coins, no dice
You make your way back to the inn, where the crew has gathered.
Captain, just in time. We got something worth discussin'.
You try not to listen, but One Eyed Wills enthusiasam is too large to ignore.
Captain, ye ain't gonna believe this, but I just heard a fat Spanish merchant ship be leave in port nearby, and it's overflowing with gold
Would you like to get supplies?
Would you like to get supplies?
Would you like to get supplies?
Captain, ye ain't gonna believe this, but I just heard a fat Spanish merchant ship be leave in port nearby, and it's overflowing with gold
Would you like to get supplies?
Would you like to get supplies?
Would you like to get supplies?
Good choice. Let's stock up on gunpowder, fresh water, and new cutlasses. Now, it's time to set sail and hunt that Spanish merchant ship
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
Are you ready to set sail?
You don't stock up on supplies. And leave instantly.

Set sail. Captain, I hope ye be right about this. The men don't like the idea of fighting on an empty stomach. I would sure like some grub right now. But there's no turning back now. Your target is on the horizon, and there be gold to claim
Are you ready to approach the spanish?
Are you ready to approach the spanish?
Are you ready to approach the spanish?
A few days into the voyage, the ship sails smooth—but below deck, Mad jack is complaining.
Captain, this ain't a pirate ship. This be a floating prison. No tropical punch, no joy, no adventure. Arrr.
Captain, he's got a point. The crew are growing weary.
We got three choices. We can teach Mad Jack a lesson, we can hand out coin for tropical punch, or we can ignore the lot of them and hope they quiet down
Well, let's hear another shanty before we set sail.
Hi-dee, hi-dee, hi-dee-ho. A hi-dee-ho, a hi-dee-ho. A hi-dee, hi-dee, hi-dee-ho. Over the deep blue sea
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
A wise decision, Captain. A thirsty pirate be a dangerous pirate.
Good job, Captain. Spirits are lifted, and there's no more talk of mutiny
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Right you are, Captain. No tropical punch, no handouts. The ship runs on your command. But the crew don't seem too happy.
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Haha. Mad Jack is fast asleep. Let's play a prank with his wooden leg. Let's turn his wooden leg into a wooden flute. Show us your flute-playing skills, captain.
Hey, you woke me up. Wait, why is me leg whistling? Oh, fair enough. I guess I had that coming, Captain.
The crew is entertained, nice job. Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Here is Jack's Wooden leg flute shanty again.
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on, say yes or no.

There it is on the horizon, a big fat Spanish merchant ship . We got two choices, either we charge in, cannons blazing, or we get sneaky and switch to Spanish colors and sail right up next to 'em before they realize what's happening
Say TRICK, to use deception or FIGHT, to open fire.
Up goes our Spanish flag. Let's hope they don't notice the smell of tropical punch and gunpowder that follows us.
A Spanish officer leans over the railing, his ridiculously oversized wig wobblin' in the wind.
Buenos dias, amigos. What business brings you out this far?
Cap, this be the moment. Shall we board them peacefully and strike when close, or just fire now and take them by surprise?
Venimos a dar guerra, no besos. Load the cannons. Fire!
Dios mio! You blew the wig off my head and set it on fire.
Oh, who is this? It must be El Capitan.
I am El Capitan, and you are on my boat. Leave now or the consequences will be unforgiving
Ramp it up a notch, captain.
You got me. I know you, the captain of the Black Tide. Spare me, and I'll tell ye of an English ship carrying 10,000 gold coins
Want to hear what he has to say?
Want to hear what he has to say?
Want to hear what he has to say?
Well, let's hear another shanty before we set sail.
Hi-dee, hi-dee, hi-dee-ho. A hi-dee-ho, a hi-dee-ho. A hi-dee, hi-dee, hi-dee-ho. Over the deep blue sea
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to sail on?
Are you ready to move on?
Leaving this to the lads, are you?
Oh, dear. I yield, I yield. Take the ship, the gold. It is yours.
Aye, but the crew don't be liking a captain who shies away from a fight
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Are you ready to move on?
Shh. Shh. Yes, yes. Excellent sneaking, Captain. Jump on the ship.
The spanish crew member, still adjusting his enormous, ridiculous wig, greets you with suspicion.
I do not recognize you, señor. What is your business aboard this ship?
Would you like to fight the spanish crew member?
Would you like to fight the spanish crew member?
Would you like to fight the spanish crew member?
Instead of fighting the spaniard, the crew attempts to trick him instead.

Aye, aye, me capitan. We come on urgent tortilla orders from the governor of Havana Grande himself. Oh, there be grave problemas, my spicy, ahead, and we've been sent to escort your ship through these waters muy dangerous, oh, and possibly haunted, oh.
You sound more like a goat than a Spaniard.
An escort? We had not been informed
If you keep up the act, the spanish crew might fall for it. But if they get suspicious, things may turn ugly.
Want to try and trick him again?
Want to try and trick him again?
Want to try and trick him again?
If this is the governor's order, we must comply.
Yer crew 'inspects' the cargo hold, makin' sure to secure all the gold.
Captain, if pirating doesn't work out, you'll make a fine cottonman
Wait. Why do you smell like tropical punch and gunpowder? Ouch
One of your crew slaps him with a fish, knocking him out.
Well, Captain, you got the treasure, but maybe he had more information
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Take the gold, take the ship, but I've got something more valuable
Oh, is that so? Talk fast.
The English navy sails from Kingston in three days. 10,000 gold aboard, two warships escorting. Their captain, Commodore Hawthorne, is ruthless.
A fortune ripe for the taking, Captain
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Are you ready to sail back to the haven?
Instead of going to the haven, you take inspiration from the Spanish vessel. and pour your soul into some Flamenco music.
That was really something. Now, we really should be heading to the haven
That was beautiful. Now, do you want to go back to the haven?
Want to go to the pirate haven?
Want to go to the pirate haven?
Captain, that went smoother than I expected. The crew are happy
Hi-di, hi-di, hi-di-ho. Hi-di-ho, hi-di-ho. Hi-di, hi-di, hi-di-ho, over the deep blue sea
It's time to have some much needed relaxation at the pirate haven
Want to go to the pirate haven?
Want to go to the pirate haven?
Want to go to the pirate haven?
You veer off the beaten track, into unknown waters...
The night is calm, stars twinkling, waves gently rocking the ship. Smooth sailing at last.
Captain, something is pulling our anchor.
Oh, it's probably nothing. Uh-oh. It's the kraken. Crew, pull the anchor rope back.
By the sea gods, we're playing tug-of-war with a kraken.
Want to pull the rope harder?
Want to pull the rope harder?
Want to pull the rope harder?
You let go of the rope.
You lost your anchor rope. But atleast the kraken is happy.
Are you ready to go back to the pirate haven?
Want to sail back to the pirate haven?
Want to sail back to the pirate haven?
The kraken gave up and let go of the rope.
Did we just win tug of war against a kraken?
Want to sail back to the pirate haven?
Want to sail back to the pirate haven?
Want to sail back to the pirate haven?
As you wish, Captain. Let's sail around a bit. Oh, what's that? Just a teeny harmless raindrop. Oh dear, a storm be coming. Hold on tight.
Suddenly, you feel comfortable and safe.
The warmth of the inn welcomes ye. A roaring fire, a soft bed, and a cup of tropical punch smoother than the sea on a calm day. Sleep well, Captain.
Somehow you have awoken comfortably at the pirate haven. Want to rejoin the crew?

Dead Man's Refuge, where a pirate can live like a king, if only for a night. So, Captain, how be we spending the night? A warm bed and a belly full of tropical punch, or testing fate at the dice tables?
You can say REST, or DICE.
The warmth of the inn welcomes ye. A roaring fire, a soft bed, and a cup of tropical punch smoother than the sea on a calm day. Sleep well, Captain.
You awake, well rested. You gain 20 health, but spend 10 coins in the process.
